name: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd

items.statement: New Abu Dhabi facility for pen and auto-injectors with investment of AED130-150 million (INR300-350 crores) and capacity of 75 million units per year.
items.quote: The planned investment is in the range of AED130 million to AED150 million, translating to about INR300 crores to INR350 crores to build a capacity of approximately 75 million pen injectors -- pen/auto-injectors per year.

items.statement: Total pen injector capacity to increase to 150 million units from current 80 million units per year.
items.quote: With this addition, our total pen injector capacity will increase substantially to 150 million units from the current 80 million units per year.

items.statement: First high-speed pen assembly line operational qualification to complete next week, commercial production from March, scale-up from April.
items.quote: The first line is going through operational qualification, should be completed next week and then we'll go into supply immediately after.

items.statement: Second high-speed line to arrive end April/early May 2026, commercialized by end July 2026.
items.quote: The second line is scheduled to arrive in end of April, beginning of May '26. So it will get commercialized by end of July '26.

items.statement: Already supplying GLP-1 injectors for commercial launches in Canada, Brazil, India, Middle East, Turkey; demand exceeds supply.
items.quote: We've already started supplying in the last quarter itself for commercial launches, which are planned in Canada, Brazil, India, Middle East, Turkey.

items.statement: 10-15% price erosion seen on high-volume contracts; further erosion expected but to stabilize after first 24 months.
items.quote: We've seen essentially10% to 15% price erosion on those numbers. But that's a given. When you sit down to negotiate large volume contracts, you will see that happen anyways.

items.statement: Margins to improve in Q4, full normalization in Q1 FY27 as high-speed line ramps up.
items.quote: So margins will certainly go up in quarter 4, but you will see full normalization only in quarter 1.

items.statement: Healthcare revenue mix doubled to 42% of overall revenue.
items.quote: the Healthcare segment's contribution to our overall revenue mix, which has now doubled to 42% compared to last year, reflecting the increasing scale of this business.

items.statement: Consumer segment decline due to demand slowdown in Europe and US; rebound depends on economic recovery and trade agreements.
items.quote: we have seen some decline because of overall demand slowdown, which is happening in Europe and U.S. As and when economy improves there, I think we should see a rebound.

items.statement: Abu Dhabi facility to be funded by mix of internal accruals and debt; approaching bankers in India and Abu Dhabi.
items.quote: We basically look at funding it by a mix of internal accruals and debt. The implementation time, as Amit indicated in his opening remarks, is 18 months.

items.statement: Onboarded 2 new customers for GLP-1s and signed 2 new contracts with Global Pharma for pen injectors.
items.quote: we have onboarded 2 new customers for GLP -1s and have also additionally signed 2 new contracts with Global Pharma for the manufacture and supply of pen injectors.

items.statement: Consumer electronics qualification to end by Feb/March; supplies to begin Q4/Q1.
items.quote: We should come to an end of qualification either end of this month or early March. And hopefully, from there on, we will have a little bit more visibility on supplies.

items.statement: Semiconductor casings: in talks with all 4 fabs in Gujarat; small supplies expected in new FY, scale-up depends on fab commercialization.
items.quote: We should see some small quantities in the new FY for sure. But I think any scale -up will largely depend on how quickly these capacities come up and how quickly they then scale from after setup.

items.statement: Total PMY order 8 lakh machines; 4 lakh awarded (Singer got 70%), balance 4 lakh pending government decision.
items.quote: Yes, as I explained, the total order size was 8 lakhs, out of which 4 lakh was awarded. Another 4 lakh is likely to come in.

items.statement: Export opportunity to SVP at least 2-3 years away due to need for scale to compete on global prices.
items.quote: I do not see it earlier than the next 2 years or 3 years.

items.statement: No dividend; Board to conserve resources for growth investments.
items.quote: As of now, we are not giving any dividend, and the Board is clear that we have to be on the growth path, and we have to conserve our resources for planning for investment for growth.

items.statement: ZigZag machines grew 22% in Q3 and 31% YTD.
items.quote: The ZigZag Machine in the quarter, we have grown by 22%, and for the YTD, we have grown by 31%.

items.statement: Appliances gross margin contracted 120 bps on unfavorable mix with lower high-margin sales.
items.quote: Revenue in appliances declined by 7%, and gross margins contracted by 120 basis points, primarily due to an unfavorable product mix with lower sales of high-margin products.

items.statement: Government sales ~10-12% excluding PMY; appliances fully outsourced.
items.quote: So, apart from the PMY, our government sale is, approximately 10-12%.

items.statement: Reclaim rubber volume growth expected mid-teen in FY27 over FY26.
items.quote: expectation is a mid-teen kind of a number in terms of volume growth for next year over FY '26.

items.statement: FY27 capex for pyrolysis and recovered carbon black about INR 80 crores.
items.quote: the rest of the capex as far as FY '27 is concerned, an approximate about INR 80 crores of capex to be deployed in this year.

items.statement: FY27 capex for reclaim rubber new technology INR 12-15 crores.
items.quote: That investment is likely to be in the region of between INR 12 crores to INR 15 crores and will be deployed entirely by May of this year.

items.statement: FY26 capex spent about INR 50 crores total.
items.quote: together, close to INR 50 crores of the total capex for FY '26.

items.statement: Pyrolysis and rCB project commissioning by August 2026, commercial production from H2 FY27.
items.quote: These are now expected to be commissioned by August 2026 with commercial production available from the second half of the half year.

items.statement: New reclaim rubber technology line to be commissioned by May/June 2026.
items.quote: we have already initiated the investment and potentially by May or June of this year, that capex is likely to get commissioned as well.

items.statement: New reclaim technology utilization to reach 60-65% starting next quarter.
items.quote: I think the new tech will start seeing the utilization inch up about 60%, 65%, starting next quarter.

items.statement: Price increases effective this quarter to fully pass on raw material cost increase.
items.quote: A large part of the price increases will get effective from this quarter onwards. And hopefully, as a result, the extent of the price increase will be completely passed on.

items.statement: U.S. tariff reduction expected to improve export volumes and realizations from current quarter.
items.quote: This change is expected to improve our export volumes and realizations with benefits likely to begin reflecting from the current quarter itself.

items.statement: U.S. volume recovery expected over next few quarters, clarity in 3-4 weeks.
items.quote: we should be able to revert to those volumes potentially over the course of the next few quarters. I mean exact timing is still uncertain.

items.statement: Focus on automotive, electrical, appliances for subsidiary to improve margins.
items.quote: We're shifting or rather I wouldn't say shifting, but focusing far more on automotive, electrical and appliances sectors and that's something that we are hoping will provide long-term stability as well as improved margin.

items.statement: Subsidiary operating model reassessed; options include fundraise, strategic partnership, capital reduction.
items.quote: As far as your question on whether we are looking at either of a fundraise or a strategic partnership and or reduction in capital, I think we haven't gotten far. I mean there is all on the drawing board and several options under consideration.

items.statement: Expects 50-60% YoY growth in Design & Build for next 1-2 years.
items.quote: So we are very clear that we should be able to achieve that 50% to 60% growth target, as we have always maintained for next 1 or 2 years.

items.statement: Targets adding ~20,000 seats in FY26, with 5,000+ already in pipeline.
items.quote: We already have about more than 5,000 seats in the pipeline out of the 7,000 that we are talking, to achieve that number of around 20,000.

items.statement: Furniture capacity utilization to reach 75-80% by Q1-Q2 FY27.
items.quote: by first to second quarter maximum, we should be in a capacity of operating with a run rate of anything around 75% to 80% capacity

items.statement: Leasing segment PAT margin ~25% at corporate level.
items.quote: under Leasing vertical, it would be around odd 25%.

items.statement: Design & Build PAT margin 18-20%.
items.quote: on the Design & Build, to summarize, the PAT margin would be anything around 18 to 20%.

items.statement: Furniture expected PAT margin 20-22% once stabilized.
items.quote: on a pre-tax basis, around 25% and maybe post-tax basis, anything around 20 to 22%.

items.statement: Design & Build order book over INR 160 crores.
items.quote: for Q4, we have an order book of around INR 160 crores plus

items.statement: Average pricing per seat ~INR 7,000, margin ~INR 2,000 per seat.
items.quote: my average pricing right now is going at about 7,000 rupees. So if you apply that 30% margin, that's about 2,100 rupees per seat

items.statement: No significant impact from AI on IT-enabled services demand.
items.quote: we don't see any significant impact on that as far as we are concerned

items.statement: Owns 300,000+ sq ft; will acquire more properties as cash flow permits.
items.quote: we already have more than about 300,000 square feet under our own ownership.

items.statement: Furniture vertical scaling, backward integration to drive margins.
items.quote: As utilization improves, this vertical will contribute disproportionately to margins.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20%+; 3-5 year CAGR maintained at 15-20%
items.quote: And in terms of top line growth for next financial year, we are looking at somewhere around close to 20- plus percentage. And overall, for next 3 to 5 years, we are maintaining our guidelines of 15% to 20%.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to expand from current double-digit levels toward 12% over next two years
items.quote: So as I mentioned earlier, Ajit, I think the endeavour would be to attain a 12% EBITDA margin over the next two years or so.

items.statement: FY26 capex revised up to INR 350-400 cr from earlier INR 220-260 cr due to advancement for Bengaluru plant; FY27 capex guided at INR 100-150 cr
items.quote: Capex for the FY 26 will be INR 350 crores to INR400 crores, up from the earlier guided number of INR 220 crores to INR260 crores in our previous calls.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 1,759 cr; 81% LED-based; 60% to convert to production in FY27
items.quote: On the order book front, current order book stands at INR 1,759 crores. We have secured multiple new orders from leading OEMs across segments, further strengthening order book.

items.statement: LED share of revenue rose to 61% in Q3 from 52% YoY; 81% of order book LED-based; front lighting 69% of revenue
items.quote: LED lighting contributes over 61% of our revenue compared to 52% in the same quarter last year. We expect this share to increase further going ahead as nearly 81% of our current order book is LED-based.

items.statement: Auto industry delivered best-ever Q3: PV +19%, 2W +15%, 3W +35%, CV +18% YoY; growth driven by GST cuts, tax relief, rate cuts
items.quote: Despite Q3 being a seasonally weak period, the automotive industry has delivered its best ever third quarter. As per SIAM production data for October to December quarter, the Passenger Vehicle (PV) production stood at about 14 lakh units, up 19% year-on-year (y-o-y).

items.statement: LED/electronic lighting content per vehicle 2x-6x conventional; higher import content in electronics
items.quote: In general, because electronics has higher import content and content for vehicle in electronics-based lighting is somewhere range from 2x to 5-6x.

items.statement: One-time INR 15.9 cr impact from new labour codes in 9M FY26; tooling profitability cyclical (Q3 had ~INR 10 cr exceptional gain)
items.quote: I would like to highlight that this is after accounting for a onetime impact of INR15.9 crores related to the implementation of new labour codes.

items.statement: SL Lumax 9M revenue flat at INR 2,160 cr; FY27 outlook INR 2,700-2,800 cr
items.quote: Outlook for the current financial year, most likely they will close somewhere around INR2,700 crores to INR2,800 crores that's the outlook, but it all depends on how the market will shape up.

items.statement: New product launches contribute ~50% of FY27 guided 20%+ growth; OEM model cycles shortened to 2-3 years from 3-5 years
items.quote: I would say that close to perhaps half of that should come from the new product and the rest would be organic growth of the industry.

items.statement: Full LED headlamp mass adoption long haul due to cost and import-dependent LED modules; projector lamps may penetrate faster on 2W
items.quote: It definitely can, but I personally still feel that it's going to be pretty long haul as LED as a full LED headlamp to become mass market because, again, the cost and the economies just don't work out.

items.statement: Air navigation system opportunity ~INR500 crores over 3-5 years; first order INR30 crores from GRSE already received.
items.quote: We estimate that, again, the total opportunity is again to the tune of about INR 500 crores or so, again, in 3- to 5-year kind of time horizon of order booking.

items.statement: Defense and space programs expected to achieve 20-25% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: The margins for these programs, obviously, I would categorize it just generally to say that in this business, we expect to be at 20% to 25% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Space-based surveillance opportunity ~INR1,000 crores; orders expected in Q4 and subsequent quarters.
items.quote: As I said, total opportunity size is there in the range of about INR 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Semiconductor equipment customer expected to generate at least $10 million in FY26, scaling to $30 million annual run rate in 2 years.
items.quote: We expect, as I mentioned earlier, that on -- in this financial year, we expect to do at least $10 million of business, if not more, which was practically zero in the past year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved 200 bps in 9M FY26; expect steady improvement in coming years.
items.quote: You've seen already, as we mentioned, in the 9-month period, EBITDA margins have improved by about 200 basis points at the standalone level.

items.statement: Q4 expected to be a bigger quarter; margins to be maintained or improved.
items.quote: Typically, Q4 for us is a bigger quarter also. So we will maintain or improve our margins in Q4.

items.statement: No further material financial impact expected from overseas restructuring beyond what is recognized.
items.quote: Based on our present assessment, we do not expect any further material financial impact beyond what has already been recognized.

items.statement: French subsidiary divestment unlikely to realize meaningful value; judicial reorganization may take 4-6 months.
items.quote: Based on our assessment today, we don't expect to realize anything meaningful from this divestment.

items.statement: Increased defense spending in Europe/Israel driving higher EMS order book; expected to continue for next few years.
items.quote: We have seen on our EMS side of the business, an increased order book coming from some of these customers.

items.statement: BTS order execution cycle 2-2.5 years; EMS less than 12 months.
items.quote: Typically order execution cycle on the BTS side of the business would be typically in the range of about 2 to 2.5 years. So whereas on the EMS side of the business, it's a lot more shorter, maybe less than 12 months.

items.statement: EMS business sustainable long-term EBITDA margin around 10-11%.
items.quote: The EMS business in these type of sectors are typically around the 10%, 11% EBITDA levels.

items.statement: Defense and space business expected to grow multifold in coming years; no specific guidance provided.
items.quote: We have strong objectives of growing this multifold in the coming years. I won't specify exactly a number in terms of guidance or anything like that.

items.statement: Virupaksha order won; development orders currently small, production could be hundreds of crores.
items.quote: Yes, we won the order and the programs are in execution.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for the year maintained at 25-26%.
items.quote: we would still hold ourselves for the year what we have started the year with 25% to 26.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR 500-600 crore, subject to board approval.
items.quote: So broadly, it will be about INR 500 crore to INR 600 crore. And obviously, once we get through the whole process after Board approval, we will give you proper guidance next quarter.

items.statement: Order book stands at $1.2 billion as of Q3 FY26.
items.quote: And as of this quarter, we are in the range of $1.2 billion of order book.

items.statement: 8-10 new molecules to be commercialized, 5 already done.
items.quote: We are on track to commercialize 8 to 10 new molecules with 5 molecules already commercialized.

items.statement: Pioxaniliprole registration expected in next financial year, first Indian innovation in AgChem.
items.quote: within the next financial year, we should be achieving the registration. So that means a landmark in Indian history and the first Indian innovation in Ag-chem, Pioxaniliprole, will be commercialised in the coming financial year.

items.statement: CSM business expected to turn positive in FY27, with green shoots in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: we are already seeing a positive traction and have started showing certain green shoots. We are pretty confident it will turn positive in FY27.

items.statement: Working capital days increased to 139, expected to improve as market normalizes.
items.quote: Our trade working capital in terms of days of sales has increased to 139 days and reflects current market conditions, we expect to improve this as market scenario normalizes in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Biologicals contribution around 20% in FY26 so far.
items.quote: It is around 20 odd percent.

items.statement: Unitec JV total capex INR110 crores; production in 15-18 months.
items.quote: Our JV is a total cluster of INR110 crores, okay. And it would -- we've already started the building and we've ordered out the longest length, I would say equipment. And that would be a period of 12 months before it's received. It would take another few months to stabilize. So I would say it would be 15 to 18 months by

items.statement: Board sanctioned INR270 crores capex; INR100 crores for new plan; staggered over 2-2.5 years.
items.quote: So right now this capex would take us approximately 2-2.5 years, right? So the number still stays.

items.statement: Mahant Toolroom order book over INR25 crores; average turnover ~INR2 crores.
items.quote: So the average turnover is approximately INR2 crores, but they received very large orders from HAL and other customers, which are conservatively placed at INR25 crores after a lot of due diligence, taking into account that some platforms come faster and some platforms take a little longer.

items.statement: Industrial segment growing faster, now 11-12% of total; CV 27-30%, 2W/3W 30%, aftermarket 10-12%, PV 20%.
items.quote: So I can tell you roughly the CV segment for us is 27% to 30%. The two and three wheeler segment is again another 30%. Industrial is growing faster but out of the total pie, it is roughly been 8% to 10% and now is starting to move faster to 11%, 12%.

items.statement: Aftermarket demand weak; company not dependent due to OEM focus.
items.quote: Aftermarket is definitely down. There's no question. Overall the aftermarket is facing very challenging situations and that is probably one of the reasons you've seen our competitors having a great deal of challenge.

items.statement: US business down 4-5%, impacting exports; otherwise domestic/export mix would be 70/30.
items.quote: Right now it's 75/25 because we are 4% to 5% business from the U.S. which is to the extent that the U.S business is down. Otherwise it would have been 70/30.

items.statement: Plans to enter larger spherical, cylindrical, taper bearings in next 12 months.
items.quote: See, what I explained last time is we are planning to enter the bearing market for larger spherical, cylindrical, and taper bearings, but that will be a separate phase. When we do it, we'll announce it with all the data. Right now, it is not a market that we are currently in. It's something we plan to do in the next 12

items.statement: No future guidance; company aims to outperform stated targets.
items.quote: We are very aggressive, but we don't tend to give guidance. So we tend to like to perform beyond what we state. And I think it's just a company culture.

items.statement: Maintains 15-20% revenue growth for FY26; expects better in FY27, including defense.
items.quote: Our perception towards the market is that our prediction for the 15% to 20% growth, it remains the same. As in this year, it could not be because the prices were downside. But as you have rightly said, that now the prices have started increasing, and the markets from this December 2nd part, markets have also improved.

items.statement: Defense capacity expansion from 1.5 lakh to 4 lakh shells to cost INR400 crores, funded 60% equity, 40% debt.
items.quote: Sir, for this augmentation of capacity from 1.5 lakh to 4 lakh, we will be incurring a expense of almost a capital expenditure of almost INR400 crores. items.statement: Defense segment has 8 months order in hand and 2 years LOI; order visibility strong for next financial year.
items.quote: We have eight months order in hand and two years LOI with us. We are confident that this plan what I have envisaged now will have a bright future for us and we are bullish on defense and aerospace and all our planning.

items.statement: Defense EBITDA margin currently 30%, expected to rise to 30-35% next year.
items.quote: Expected revenue, right now, between 150,000 capacity, expected revenue is INR300 crores. And with the augmented capacity, the revenue will be almost INR900 crores and the EBITDA margins will be almost 30% right now, and we hope it will go in the range of 30% to 35% in the coming year as well.

items.statement: Steel price hikes impact input costs; auto tubes pass-through with 2-quarter lag, infrastructure full pass-through, defense minimal impact.
items.quote: So basically, whenever the prices go up, it definitely impacts our input cost. But as you have said, we are in the value addition sector. items.statement: Hydraulic tube capacity utilization at 40-45%, expected to reach 60-65% in next two quarters due to easing US tariffs.
items.quote: Capacity utilization of hydraulic tubes, it is running around 40% to 45% right now. But in the coming two quarters as the U.S. tariffs has eased, so we hope that in the next two quarters, it should go almost 60% to 65% because what the easiness that Trump has given, it will pervade in the system.

items.statement: Value-added mix currently 56-60%, expected to increase to 60-65% next year.
items.quote: Right now, it extends from 56% to 60%. And in the coming year, we hope it should go from 60% to 65%.

items.statement: Defense revenue expected INR60-70 crores in Q4 FY26, full contribution from Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Yes, it is likely to be. And we hope almost INR60 crores, INR70 crores will be contributed in Q4 as well. But from Q1, it will be contributing fully.

items.statement: Solar structures business expected to reach INR600-700 crores next year.
items.quote: And this year we have done almost a very good business and next year we hope we should cross INR600 crores to INR700 crores business in this sunrise sector of the solar structures.

items.statement: Capex incurred INR186 crores till Dec 31; Q4 FY26 expected INR30 crores.
items.quote: Total capex already done till 31st December was INR186 crores. And in four th quarter, we expect about INR30 crores capex.

items.statement: Defense production awaiting government dispatch permission; if delayed, still expects INR60 crores this financial year.
items.quote: We are very much in the line, but the issue is because it needs some permission to dispatch. So we are waiting for the dispatch permission. And as I have already told that even it comes delayed, so we will be doing almost INR60 crores this financial year.

items.statement: Working capital requirement for defense at peak revenue expected INR200-250 crores.
items.quote: We expect almost INR200 crores, INR 250 crores working capital will be required at that time when we reach the peak.

items.statement: Defense demand strong; global 155mm shell demand outstripping supply, no dull demand next 4-5 years.
items.quote: So there is clearly a gap of this arms and ammunition, particularly 155 mm. So I see no dulls of demand in the next 4, 5 years.

items.statement: Aerospace EBITDA margin expected 28-32%, may improve in near future.
items.quote: As far as EBITDA margins are concerned, they are 28% to 32% -- they are what we expect right now because India is more and more pressing on the air.

items.statement: Expects FY27 revenue growth of around 10%.
items.quote: we expect FY '27 to see around 10% growth in the revenue

items.statement: Guides FY27 EBITDA margin around 13%.
items.quote: Margins around 13%. Correct.

items.statement: Confident of securing INR 8,000-10,000 crores new orders in coming year.
items.quote: we remain confident of achieving our annual order inflow target while maintaining margin discipline. So next year -- next 1 year, we expect to around addition of around INR 8,000 crores to INR 10,000 crores of new orders.

items.statement: Expects INR 7,000-8,000 crores order inflow in next 6 months.
items.quote: we say another next 6 months, we expect to get around INR7,000 crores to INR 8,000 crores order.

items.statement: Expects FY26 revenue to cross INR 5,000 crores.
items.quote: revenue as guided earlier, we expect to cross INR 5,000 crores this year.

items.statement: Capex of INR 100-150 crores required for current EPC projects.
items.quote: Yes, INR100, INR150 crores capex will be required for all the current coming up EPC projects.

items.statement: Order book as of Dec 31, 2025 stands at INR 15,123 crores.
items.quote: As of 31st December 2025, our order book stands at INR15,123 crores, providing strong multiyear visibility.

items.statement: Bids worth INR 12,000 crores under evaluation, expected to open in coming months.
items.quote: We have bids worth approximately INR12,000 crores, which are under evaluation and expected to open in the coming months.

items.statement: Identified pipeline of over INR 50,000 crores to bid in next 1 year.
items.quote: there is an identified pipeline of over INR 50,000 crores to come up bidding in the next 1 year.

items.statement: Rights issue proceeds: INR 100 crores for general corporate purposes, balance for debt repayment.
items.quote: So INR100 crores was for general corporate purpose, and the balance was for debt.

items.statement: Faced aggressive pricing in large tenders, chose not to compromise margins.
items.quote: in a few large tenders, pricing turned very aggressive, at we choose not to compromise on margin for this standard, particularly and technically complex hydro and underground projects.

items.statement: Focus remains on hydropower and pump storage projects.
items.quote: our primary focus continues to be on hydropower and pump storage projects, which forms the core of our expertise.

items.statement: Gongri BOOT project expected to generate INR 300 crores annual revenue after completion.
items.quote: After completing the project, we expect to get a revenue of around INR300 crores per annum

items.statement: Plans to reduce share pledges after March results.
items.quote: Time line-wise, post this March results, we are -- we'll start talking to the lenders.

items.statement: Management expects at least 25% growth in FY27.
items.quote: But that said, I think FY '27, you can expect at least a 25% growth.

items.statement: Board approved raising up to INR 500 crores via NCDs on private placement.
items.quote: On the liquidity and capital front, the Board has approved raising up to INR 500 crores through NCDs on a private placement basis, providing us with additional financial flexibility to support future growth.

items.statement: Target opex ratio of 4.5% to 5% of AUM for Microfinance consolidated.
items.quote: I would love for them to at about 4.5%. Well, for Microfinance consol level, let's say, about probably 4.5% to about 5% of total AUM.

items.statement: Non-JLG products to grow much faster than JLG; JLG growth slower or flat.
items.quote: I would say the non-JLG will grow much, much faster, whether that is in the subsidiary, Namra, or in the stand-alone Arman through MSME, LAP and two-wheeler loans. So I would say JLG will be a lot slower to or even I dare to say, growth and while these other products will continue to grow faster.

items.statement: GNPA likely to decrease further in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: My judgment tells me that, yes, definitely, in Q4, it should go down further.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 shaping up better than Q3.
items.quote: Q4 seems to be shaping up even better.

items.statement: Solar loan pilot targeting INR 1 crore monthly disbursement by March.
items.quote: The goal is in this quarter to reach about INR1 crores of disbursement monthly by March, hopefully.

items.statement: May offer lower interest rates to customers using cashless payments.
items.quote: So yes, I think if a customer is paying a significant amount of their EMIs through cashless mechanisms, definitely, we can pass on some rate benefit.

items.statement: GNPA unlikely to go below 3% in long run on average.
items.quote: But where the industry stands today, it would be hard for me to say, we will ever go below 3%, for example.

items.statement: MSME portfolio can scale 20-25% without increasing opex.
items.quote: Maybe by about 20 %-25% for sure, we can scale up without increasing opex.

items.statement: LAP portfolio could surpass MSME in 2-3 years.
items.quote: And yes, over 2, 3 years, I think it's definitely possible for it to even surpass the MSME portfolio for the reasons which I said.

items.statement: Past defaulters auto-rejected, reducing customer pool; rejection rate improved to 75-77%.
items.quote: The rejection rate has improved slightly by 2%, 3%, where it was, let's say, about 80% earlier, now it is closer to 75%-77%.

items.statement: 82% of MFI portfolio covered under CGFMU scheme.
items.quote: As of December 2025, 82% of our MFI portfolio is covered under the CGFMU scheme providing an additional year of risk protection and balance sheet comfort.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity target: first milestone 3-3.5x, comfortable up to 4.5x.
